title: Console: regional failover banner + status widget (Hosted API + Dedicated)
creator: Marissa Cole
description:
Goal
Design Console UI elements that clearly communicate: (1) real regional impairment, (2) active failover/traffic shifting, and (3) planned failover tests (“game days”)—with minimal confusion and without leaking sensitive internal signals.

We need two surfaces:
1) A global banner (top of Console) for time-sensitive events.
2) A status widget (dashboard card) on the Console Overview page, with deeper detail in a dedicated “Service Status” view.

Primary users
- Hosted API customers (self-serve + enterprise) looking to understand incident impact and mitigations.
- Dedicated customers (SRE/Platform teams) needing clarity on pool drain, routing, and expected behavior.
- Internal CSM/Support using Console as source of truth for what customers will see.

Non-goals
- Replace the public status page.
- Show raw trigger signals (burn rates, reachability graphs) directly in customer UI.
- Per-request debugging UX (handled elsewhere).

Design principles
- Clarity over completeness: convey “what you should do” and “what to expect” in <10 seconds.
- Separate “planned test” vs “incident” language with unmistakable labels.
- Avoid flapping UI: reflect controller state changes with hold-down and human-friendly timestamps.
- Tenant-aware: Dedicated + Hosted have different artifacts; enterprise tiers may have residency constraints.

Proposed information architecture
A) Global banner (always visible)
- Shows only when one of these states is true:
  1) Regional Incident (customer-impacting or likely) OR
  2) Active Failover / Traffic Shift in progress OR
  3) Planned Failover Test window (only for scoped tenants/regions)
- Banner variants:
  - Severity: Info (planned), Warning (degradation), Critical (outage/failover)
  - Copy includes: short headline, affected product(s), region(s), “last updated”, CTA(s)
- CTAs (priority order):
  - “View status details” (internal Console page)
  - “View status page” (public) (only for incidents; optional for planned tests)
  - “Contact support” (enterprise accounts; otherwise link to docs/support portal)

B) Status widget (Overview card)
- Default state: “All systems operational” + last check timestamp.
- Degraded state: show affected product(s) and region chips.
- Failover state: show “Traffic shifting” with progress language (not percent-based unless backend provides stable milestones).
- Dedicated-specific: show per-pool note when a customer’s dedicated pool is in drain/evacuation workflow.
- Click-through to details: timeline + FAQ.

Event taxonomy (customer-facing)
We need customer-facing labels that map to internal controller states without exposing sensitive details.
- Operational: no issues
- Degraded performance: elevated errors or latency (not necessarily failover)
- Regional incident: confirmed impairment in a region
- Failover in progress: active traffic shifting away from impacted region
- Failover complete: traffic shifted; monitoring ongoing
- Planned failover test: scheduled exercise with limited blast radius

Copy guidelines (draft)
- Prefer “traffic shifting” vs “failover automation triggered” (avoid implying unsafe automation).
- Avoid “burn rate”, “SLO”, “circuit breaker” terms in customer UI.
- Use concrete expectations:
  - “You may see elevated latency/timeouts.”
  - “Streaming responses may reconnect.”
  - “Retry with exponential backoff.”
- For planned tests, lead with reassurance:
  - “We’re running a controlled resiliency test. No action needed. Some requests may be retried.”

Detailed UI behavior
1) Banner timing and dampening
- Banner should update only on stable state changes (align with controller hold-down timers).
- If state flips within 3 minutes, show a single consolidated message + latest timestamp (avoid rapid copy changes).

2) Multi-product mapping
- Products: Hosted API, Dedicated, Console (control plane), Other (if needed)
- Banner should list impacted products; widget shows “Your products” first.

3) Region representation
- Use region codes + friendly names (e.g., us-east (N. Virginia), eu-west (Ireland))
- If many regions: show top 2 + “+N more”

4) Dedicated nuance
- If Dedicated pool drain is happening, show:
  - “Dedicated capacity: traffic shifting”
  - “Some requests may be queued or retried”
  - CTA: “View Dedicated status” (filtered to tenant)
- Do not show other tenants’ pool names or sizes.

5) Planned test targeting
- Only show planned test banner to:
  - Tenants in scope OR
  - Internal Redwood staff
- If a tenant is explicitly excluded, do not show banner (prevents confusion).

6) Data residency / boundaries
- For regulated/residency-bound tenants: banner copy must not suggest traffic will route cross-region if policy disallows it.
- Proposed conditional line when residency constraints apply:
  - “Traffic will remain within your configured regions.”
  - If failover cannot proceed: show “Mitigation limited by configured regions; we’re working to restore service.” (needs PM sign-off)

Open questions
- What is the source-of-truth event stream for customer-facing status? (controller audit events vs a curated status service)
- Do we want per-model messaging (e.g., only certain models affected)? (risk of churn/confusion)
- Whether “subscribe to updates” belongs in Console (vs status page only).

Deliverables
- Updated banner + widget designs (Figma link in attachments)
- Final copy strings for each variant (planned/degraded/failover/outage)
- Interaction notes for engineering (states, fields required)
- Accessibility checklist (contrast, iconography, screen reader labels)

Acceptance criteria
- Customers can answer: “Is this planned or unplanned?” within one glance.
- Customers can answer: “Am I affected?” with product + region indicators.
- CTA is unambiguous and routes to more detail.
- UI does not flap more frequently than controller hold-down.
- Dedicated view shows only tenant-specific information.

Engineering notes (fields needed)
- event_type: planned_test | incident | failover
- severity: info | warning | critical
- impacted_products: hosted_api | dedicated | console
- impacted_regions: list of region codes
- tenant_scope: all | allowlist | denylist
- last_updated_at + started_at
- customer_copy_override (optional for Support to adjust copy, with audit)

Links
- Drive: failover-console-banner-mock (working copy/mocks)
- Confluence: status-page-template-regional-event (copy alignment)
- Confluence: regional-failover-communication-playbook
- Linear: PM-512 (customer-facing expectations)
comments: 2026-01-06 — Marissa Cole (Creator/PM): Creating design ticket to lock customer-facing language and UI behaviors before we enable production game day banners. Please coordinate with Support/CS on wording (planned vs incident).

2026-01-08 — Nora Ahmed (Assignee): Drafted initial banner hierarchy: Planned Test (blue), Degraded (amber), Failover/Outage (red). Biggest risk is UI flapping during noisy signals; proposing alignment with hold-down timers and only showing curated “state” rather than metrics.

2026-01-09 — Chloe Martin (Console backend): We can provide a single “customer_status” object per tenant with event_type/severity/regions/started_at/updated_at. We should avoid exposing internal region-health reason codes. If you need progress, we can add discrete milestones (initiated -> shifting -> stabilized).

2026-01-12 — Devon Price (Incident-bot/tooling): FYI we’ll be emitting audit events for failover actions; could be used to populate the timeline view. But those events contain internal fields—recommend a separate “public projection” layer for Console/Status.

2026-01-13 — Owen Phillips (Support liaison): Strong preference that Console copy matches status page wording. Also: for planned tests, we need a line explaining what customers should do if they see errors (retry/backoff). Please avoid any phrasing that reads like an outage (“incident”) during a game day.

2026-01-14 — Allison Grant (Observability): If you want a “last checked” time, we can provide a stable timestamp from the status projection service. Please don’t poll raw signals for this widget; it’ll cause confusion when metrics lag.

2026-01-16 — Nora Ahmed: Iteration v2: added explicit pill “Planned test” vs “Incident” next to headline. Added region chips with “+N more” behavior. Also added conditional line for residency-constrained tenants (needs Security/PM sign-off).

2026-01-17 — Simran Kaur (Private deployments): For customers with strict residency boundaries, please don’t say “we are routing traffic to another region” unless you can guarantee their configuration allows it. Recommend neutral phrasing: “We are mitigating impact. Traffic remains within your configured regions.”

2026-01-20 — Marissa Cole: Agree on neutral residency phrasing. Also want a very clear CTA ladder: first “View status details” in Console, second “View status page”. For enterprise tenants, add “Contact support” (but keep it behind plan checks).

2026-01-23 — Nora Ahmed: Added Dedicated-specific tile inside the status details page (“Dedicated capacity status”) that appears only if impacted_products includes dedicated. It does not show pool identifiers; it references “your reserved capacity” + timestamps.

2026-02-01 — Ravi Menon (Routing policy TL): Please ensure we don’t imply immediate resolution on “Failover complete”. There are stabilization periods; suggest wording “Traffic shifted; monitoring continues” and keep banner visible for 30–60 minutes after completion.

2026-02-03 — Nora Ahmed: Updated copy accordingly; added “Monitoring continues” and a post-complete cool-down. Marking as In Review for Design + PM sign-off; next step is to confirm engineering field availability and finalize string table.
